contradictions.tension: Own the number vs. own the noun — and the site's own structured data currently argues for a third, retired company.
contradictions.sideA: THE GREATS (category-creation) says do not run a category campaign. Category creation is a sales-enablement mechanism executed by companies with working demand capture; Muntin has zero confirmed users and 4 waitlist forms across 1,327 pages. The transferable HubSpot asset was the definitional substrate (Website Grader, the book, the Academy), not the label. 'Own the number, not the noun' — the thing Nielsen, Case-Shiller and Moody's actually own is a named, dated, methodologically-published reading. It further argues that a model's definition of a term is fixed by corroboration across independent domains, which makes self-published DefinedTerm markup and llms.txt 'the least effective available way to buy the thing it is buying.'
contradictions.sideB: THE BONES record heavy sunk investment in exactly the noun: 691 HTML files carry DefinedTerm markup, plus llms.txt (45KB), llms-full.txt (681KB) and feed-llm.json (376KB) at the repo root. THE GREATS (branded-index, traffic-engine) also want a number but cannot agree which one — branded-index wants a stipulated dollar-denominated reference plate ('a stated recipe is a definition that cannot be wrong, while a weighted composite is an empirical claim that can'), traffic-engine wants a named index level ('Muntin Restaurant Cost Index, August 2026: 103.4, base 100'). Both call theirs the citation unlock.
contradictions.whyItMatters: Measured this session: 'restaurant cost intelligence' appears in exactly 2 HTML files of 1,327, and `/for/restaurants/` — the page carrying the category DefinedTerm — has 0 inbound internal links in `data/link-graph.json`. Meanwhile 123 of 172 glossary pages carry retired-line web-design vocabulary (`retiredLineScore >= 1`), so the DefinedTermSet a retrieval pipeline ingests says, by majority, that this is a restaurant-website-SEO company. Resolving toward the noun means a glossary re-base and more schema. Resolving toward the number means a founder call that is permanent and unrevisable — the reference plate's recipe or the index base period must be frozen forever — and it changes what every one of the 143 EN cost-index pages is FOR. Choosing neither leaves the current state, which is an internally false schema claim (`inDefinedTermSet` pointing at a glossary entry that does not exist) shipped across 691 files.

contradictions.tension: Michelin, Bloomberg, or the operating system — the foundations describe three different companies, and each implies a different answer to 'is the Cost Index the company?'
contradictions.sideA: THE GREATS (free-authority) is Michelin: the free editorial product's independence IS the revenue mechanism. 'The Cost Index's job is not to advertise Muntin Ledger, it is to make an operator start asking am I paying above the market — a question only their own invoice data can answer, which is what Ledger is.' The methodology page's firewall clause ('no Ledger relationship can move a published reading') is the anonymous-inspector clause, already mechanized. Under this reading the Index is a marketing asset with an ethical spine, and the product is the business.
contradictions.sideB: THE GREATS (branded-index) is Bloomberg/Morningstar: the instrument IS the product — mint DOIs, build `/press/`, ship a track-record page, repair the cadence, sell depth and adjacency. THE BONES (lens-upside) goes further and names two paths to a first dollar that need zero product and zero billing code: 'a paid monthly read over the free index, and paid cost work inside the founder's own vendor network.' And THE GREATS (small-team-scale) proposes a third company entirely: 'if the operating system above works, the operating system itself is the venture story, more so than the restaurant tool.'
contradictions.whyItMatters: These are not emphases, they are different companies with different first hires, different cadence obligations and different capital needs. Michelin says the Index must stay free and firewalled and every hour on it is justified by product pull-through — which makes the 4 editions in `data/cost-index-editions.json` (last 2026-07-06) a marketing lapse. Bloomberg says the same 4 editions are the product failing to ship, and that a paid read over free data is available because the methodology forecloses only placement and influence, not analysis or service. The OS reading says the restaurant tool is the demo. It also decides whether the 97.6% reconstructed backfill matters: as a marketing asset the depth is fine; as the product, only the 2,025 live-captured points since 2026-05-01 are the thing being sold.

contradictions.tension: The archive is the only genuinely unfabricatable asset, and it is the one asset the agent workforce cannot maintain.
contradictions.sideA: THE GREATS (free-authority, branded-index) and THE BONES (lens-upside) agree the moat is not the 33,523 points but the unbroken live-capture chain: 'retire coverage breadth as a growth metric and put cadence integrity in its place'; 'every exemplar that survives — Big Mac since 1986, Case-Shiller, VIX — survives on unbroken cadence, and the reason is not discipline theater: a citer's first check is is this still being published.' Every month of unbroken capture widens a gap a competitor cannot backfill.
contradictions.sideB: THE BONES (lens-capacity, CLAUDE.md) record that the live fetch requires the founder's Mac and the `FRED_KEY`/`BLS_KEY`/`AMS_KEY` secrets — 'the container has neither' — and that `build-ingredient-state-record` cannot be cleared from a container at all. 26 of 100 series are already frozen 58–88 days; the 8 ADR-013 government datasets registered as a recurring monthly chore were fetched exactly once, ever (2026-07-24). Roughly 3 of 31 maintenance-hours due were paid in the 30 days to 2026-08-07 (~10%). The free-authority panel concedes it directly: unfreezing the 26 series 'is founder-blocked work that no agent can do.'
contradictions.whyItMatters: Every other recommendation in every foundation is agent-executable; this one is not. So the resolution is a hard fork. Either the fetch moves onto a scheduled runner with secrets — which converts the company's most-guarded credential boundary into an automation surface and is a founder security decision nobody has framed as one — or the frozen series get reclassified as `withheld` with a stated reason, which is on-brand but permanently truncates the compounding record, or the cadence keeps breaking while the panels keep recommending amplification of a record that is decaying. The clock is dated: the builder cliff starts dropping ingredients in 43–62 days, and two frozen series (shrimp, vegetable-oil) are basket contributors, which is why `basket.asOf` reads 2026-06-01.

contradictions.tension: Every proposed mechanism is a new obligation, in a company already 2.7x over capacity on obligations it does not pay.
contradictions.sideA: THE OPERATING SYSTEM proposes roughly 40 new components across 8 panels — a contract compiler, a rules registry, an adherence eval, a memory budget gate, a harvest scanner, a gate-mutation harness with a mutant registry, a number-binding classifier, a citation address minter, a sunset gate, an obligations registry, a queue with per-item verifies, a role/write-permission split, a review-surface ledger, a protected-path ledger, a calibrated sampler, a comprehension probe, three recurring agent jobs. Nearly every one is costed at '1 agent session,' i.e. near-zero founder-hours to build.
contradictions.sideB: THE BONES (lens-capacity) prices standing obligations at ~53 founder-hours/month against 13–26 available, with maintenance alone at 31.2 h/mo = 1.6x capacity, and ~10% of the maintenance ledger actually paid. THE GREATS (small-team-scale) is blunter: 'Muntin did not build 1,368 pages, it built 1,368 obligations,' and 'adding a gate is now negative-value by default' (320 checks, 56 tautologies, 37.5% phantom reds). THE OPERATING SYSTEM contradicts itself here: os-evals proposes one-in-one-out funding ('an eval may only be added against a named check-all retirement') while os-advance, os-factory and os-agent-safety propose ~25 additions with no retirements named.
contradictions.whyItMatters: Build cost is not the constraint; carrying cost is. Each registry (mutants, obligations, rules, protected paths, MANUAL builders, waivers) is a hand-curated file that goes stale and reds a deploy. The company has one precedent for actually retiring something — the 13 `/course/` idem entries removed 2026-07-29 'because the gate demanded it' — which suggests retirement only happens when a gate forces it, which is itself a new mechanism. If the resolution is one-in-one-out, roughly 25 of the OS's proposals never get built and the panels must rank themselves. If it is not, the 53 h/mo becomes ~70 and the ~10% payment rate becomes ~7%, and the new machinery decays exactly like the warrant canary (89 days unsigned) and the transparency report (37 days late).

contradictions.tension: Decay must fail the deploy, or it never happens — vs. decay must never be a red, because red is a spent currency.
contradictions.sideA: THE OPERATING SYSTEM (os-memory) is categorical: 'Decay must fail the deploy, or it does not happen.' Its evidence is a natural experiment inside this company — the board's compaction policy was written into its own header, four compactions were performed, and the store still grew 5.9x in fourteen days; policy-as-chore lost 3 of 3 measured, while the enforced analogue (`check-idem-coverage`'s MANUAL registry) forced the `/course/` entries out on 2026-07-29 because the gate demanded it. 'Same company, same month, opposite outcomes — the only difference is whether it reds the deploy.'
contradictions.sideB: THE OPERATING SYSTEM (os-gate-grounding) is equally categorical and directly opposed: 'Decay must not be implemented as a red, because alarm-channel credibility is a measurable, spendable resource.' It reproduced the phantom rate (7 idem reds locally, 3 healed by the deploy, 43%) and argues red is already inflated here, so hygiene enforcement must be paid in a different channel — 'a silent automatic demotion plus a monthly digest — while the alarm channel is reserved for facts that are actually false.' It names this as why the 2026-07-30 pass shipped 14 gate commits and moved the close rate zero points: 'it added enforcement to a channel that had already stopped being read.'
contradictions.whyItMatters: This is the same foundation reaching opposite conclusions from the same measured facts, and it decides the shape of every retirement mechanism proposed anywhere in the register. If decay reds the deploy, the founder's only feedback loop absorbs more noise and the phantom rate climbs — and PR #536 already merged with three accepted reds, which os-agent-safety calls 'the first observable symptom of cognitive surrender.' If decay is a silent demotion plus a digest, it joins the four cron workflows that already open Issues and that no session has ever been pointed at — a queue with no reader is what the company has already built four times. There is a possible synthesis (red for facts that are false, demote for obligations that are stale) but nobody has written it, and the two panels each claim their rule is the general one.

contradictions.tension: Point scheduled sessions at a queue and let the machine work the gaps — vs. cap merge volume at the founder's review capacity and deliberately slow the workforce down.
contradictions.sideA: THE OPERATING SYSTEM (os-factory, os-layer-diagnosis) and THE GREATS (small-team-scale) all want more autonomous throughput: 'work at Muntin is not a rate, it is an impulse that exists only while a session is running, while decay runs on all 60 days'; the fix is 'to make the machine produce reviewable units during the gaps and reduce the founder's job to yes/no.' The four diff-and-issue crons already exist and 'every one of them stops at the Issue, because no scheduled agent session has ever been pointed at the queue.' os-layer-diagnosis wants exactly three recurring agent jobs with zero conditional edges.
contradictions.sideB: THE OPERATING SYSTEM (os-agent-safety) wants the opposite and says so explicitly: 'Throttle merge volume by review capacity rather than maximizing agent throughput: a fixed weekly review budget in reviewed-LOC, with anything that does not fit blocked from merge.' Agents added 41,293 hand-authored lines to the storefront in 33 days and 238,706 to the product in 60, against one human code commit in each window — 'agent output beyond what you can review is not throughput, it is unreviewed liability, and 72 live falsehoods on the flagship post is what that liability looks like when a stranger calls it.' It names the factory panel's own plan as a live risk: 'your stated next move is to point scheduled sessions at an Issue queue anyone on the internet can write to.'
contradictions.whyItMatters: The two prescriptions cannot both be first. Accelerating raises the unreviewed surface in a company where the founder has never run his own product and where 80–84% of commits are already Claude-authored; throttling means the 24-of-60 zero-commit days stay empty and decay keeps running on all 60. The safety panel offers a bridge — patch-shape compression collapses agent PRs 12–33x and discriminates (PR #525 refused to compress at 1,399 files → 432 shapes) — so a partial resolution is 'accelerate production, but only behind a compression-based review gate and an untrusted-input quarantine that lands BEFORE the first scheduled session touches a public Issue queue.' Nobody has sequenced that, and the queue-worker proposals currently assume the safety layer does not exist.

contradictions.tension: The contract does not load into the workforce — and nearly every proposed remedy is a line written into the contract.
contradictions.sideA: THE OPERATING SYSTEM (os-claude-md) measured it: of 56 unique agent sessions in this engagement, exactly 1 had a CLAUDE.md injected, despite 37 running with cwd = the storefront repo root. 'The workforce is workflow subagents, and workflow subagents do not load the contract.' Every rule actually followed was followed because the orchestrator hand-copied it into the prompt — board-read in 41/56, root-list discipline in 14/56, the fact gate in 16/56. Measured value: P(sees CLAUDE.md) = 1.8% vs up to 73% for a hand-copied prompt line, making routing a ~40x larger lever than content.
contradictions.sideB: THE OPERATING SYSTEM's other panels keep prescribing writes to that same file as the enforcement mechanism: os-gate-grounding component 3 ('the rule belongs in CLAUDE.md in one line') and component 8 ('Two CLAUDE.md lines and one authoring rule — the cheapest component, and the one that stops the recurrence'); os-agent-safety component 6 ('the branch-permission rule is 3 lines in CLAUDE.md') and component 8 ('The Never-Delegate list and its inverse, in CLAUDE.md'); os-memory C4 ('a budgeted retrieval contract in CLAUDE.md'). THE BONES add that the file's own facts have rotted — it says `scripts/` holds '~70' scripts against 380, cites '1428 pages' against 1,327, and contradicts itself within one bullet ('96 (idem) builders' and '83 builders').
contradictions.whyItMatters: If the load path is not fixed first, every 'one line in CLAUDE.md' recommendation in this register is a line that 98% of sessions never read — the panels would be writing rules into a file that functions as documentation, not governance, and would then measure adherence and conclude the rules were ignored. It also means the four foundations' many appeals to 'CLAUDE.md already says' are appeals to an instrument with a 1.8% delivery rate. And it changes what the deliverable of any strategy work IS: not a document, but a prompt-assembly step that selects scope-relevant sections mechanically. Until that exists, the safest form of any decision is a gate or a build step, not a written rule — which pushes back toward adding mechanisms, contradicting the capacity finding directly above.

contradictions.tension: The Greats spend the fact gate as the assurance that makes new publishing safe; the OS measured the fact gate as hollow.
contradictions.sideA: THE GREATS repeatedly treat the existing fact machinery as the thing that makes ambitious publishing safe. category-creation on binding the book: 'the fact gate has already vetted every number in it… Gate it on the existing fact-check machinery so the book cannot ship a claim the site cannot.' free-authority on The Refusals: 'fact-gated by the existing machinery.' CLAUDE.md calls `check-fabrications.mjs` 'the absolute fact gate.'
contradictions.sideB: THE OPERATING SYSTEM (os-advance) mutation-tested it and reported: 'I aged a tool's Last verified stamp to 2020-01-01 and check-tool-verified-stamp.mjs printed 14 tool page(s) clean; I inverted the meaning of a published security claim (never→always, We do not→We do) and check-security-claims.mjs printed all rendered + schema'd; 96 files carry a fabricated JSON-LD persona and check-fabrications.mjs prints 0 blocklist hits. One of five mutants was cleanly killed.' os-gate-grounding independently found 3 of 6 paired-mutant gates hollow, and that only 2 of 128 storefront gates change verdict when the entire corpus is aged 400 days. I re-ran `check-fabrications.mjs` this session: 0 blocklist hits, exit 0, across a corpus carrying 625 files with `"@type": "Person"` JSON-LD.
contradictions.whyItMatters: 'Gated by the fact machinery' is the warrant on which the Greats propose to bind a book, ship a serial editorial line, publish a track record and mint DOIs — i.e. to make claims permanent and citable. If the gate's mutation score is near zero, that warrant is unearned and the amplification proposals ship unverified claims into citation graphs at machine speed. The fork: build the mutation harness first (and accept that ~7 of the Greats' recommendations wait on it), or publish on the gates as they are and accept that the honesty machinery is a shape not a proof — which is precisely the failure mode the brand cannot survive, since the flagship post's own cite drawer at line 852 already tells a skeptic the files are 're-checked in CI' when `scripts/check-src-sentinel.mjs` does not exist on disk.

contradictions.tension: $19 is what sets the channel — vs. $19 is a self-imposed floor with no market evidence behind it.
contradictions.sideA: THE GREATS (restaurant-gtm) treats the price as the independent variable: 'Muntin's posted price sets its channel, and almost nobody has noticed. At $19–25/month per location, a customer is worth roughly $450–600 over two years,' which permanently forecloses field sales, inside sales, POS-dealer residuals and association sponsorship. What remains is the small set of channels where one relationship delivers many restaurants — 'six to eight restaurant-specialist bookkeeping firms, each carrying 12–25 clients.'
contradictions.sideB: THE OPERATOR (the-money) treats the price as the dependent variable and says raise it: 'independents demonstrably pay $350-500/location for a measured food-cost number, so $19 is a self-imposed floor, not a market ceiling.' The real barrier is TCO — a monthly count costs $100–150 of floor labor — so 'cutting price does nothing and raising it costs almost nothing.' It proposes splitting: a $19–25 Decoder tier as acquisition, and $79–149/location for the measured-food-cost tier. THE OPERATOR (incumbent-customer) agrees: '$19 was set against a scanner's value before inventory, recipes, variance and food cost shipped.'
contradictions.whyItMatters: If price is the independent variable, the bookkeeper channel is settled and everything downstream (certification for bookkeepers, the Hubdoc-replacement content lane, a firm entity, the missing `/cockpit` route) is the roadmap. If price is dependent, raising the food-cost tier to $79–149 reopens channels the GTM panel foreclosed and changes who the product is built for. Separately and independently of that fork, the UNIT is broken in code today: Solo and Team are `per_account` with no location cap while the founding rate is `per_location`, so a three-location founding member pays $57/mo against a $25 list tier with unlimited locations — the discount becomes a penalty at two locations. And `pricing-constants.ts` flags $19 as `billable: false` with no SKU, no `trial_period_days`, and checkout quantity keyed on seats, against a locked paid-GA of 2026-11-13 and a 'three months free' term that lands the first charge in mid-February, the second-worst cash month on the repo's own Census MARTS seasonality.

contradictions.tension: The bookkeeper is the only channel the price can afford, cannot be a customer in the data model, and is the exact person who will catch the number being wrong.
contradictions.sideA: THE GREATS (restaurant-gtm, category-creation) and THE OPERATOR (the-day, spanish-operator) all converge on the accounting firm: QuickBooks ProAdvisor and Dext Practice are working proofs that firms carry back-office tools into dozens of small businesses at near-zero vendor cost; Muntin already has an `accountant` role, a $150 + $30/seat tier, a `hasCockpit: true` entitlement and a shipping weekly accountant digest. category-creation wants certification built for bookkeepers and explicitly never for operators, because 'each certified bookkeeper carries Muntin's vocabulary into 10–40 restaurants.'
contradictions.sideB: THE OPERATOR (the-decision) found the channel is structurally closed: `stripe_subscriptions.org_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES orgs(id)` makes the restaurant the billing subject, `owner` is the only role that cannot be invited, and `accountant` is a guest the restaurant invites — 'so a bookkeeping firm structurally cannot be a customer, only a permission.' Confirmed this session: no `/cockpit` route exists in `apps/web` — the entitlement is sold and the surface is missing. THE OPERATOR (domain-correctness) adds the harder objection: the number that tier exists to print is biased low three ways, 'and the accounting firm is the exact buyer who will ask does this include the other location's invoices, and where is my catch-weight meat? … one relationship carries many restaurants — which means one bad number does not cost one customer, it costs the whole book.'
contradictions.whyItMatters: The three findings are sequential, not parallel, and nobody has sequenced them. Opening the channel requires (a) a `firms` entity plus a client-org edge plus firm-billed Stripe — after fixing the `billing.ts:174-175` seat multiplication, which on a per-client quantity model would bill a 20-client firm ~$3,000/month; (b) the Purchases-leg correctness work, including a location predicate that `inventory-purchases-store.ts:19-20` documents as absent while counts are per-location; and (c) Don personally calling ~20 firms, which no agent can do. domain-correctness names the protective irony explicitly: 'Zero confirmed users after fifteen months is currently protecting the company from this; opening the channel removes that protection.' The alternative resolution — sell the Decoder to operators direct and defer the firm entirely — abandons the only channel arithmetic that closes at the posted price.

contradictions.tension: Maximize the storefront for traffic and confidence now — vs. the number is wrong and the honesty debt is a multiplier on every amplification win.
contradictions.sideA: THE ENGAGEMENT's stated interim goal, and most of THE GREATS, point at storefront amplification ahead of the product: ship 82 embeds, mint DOIs, build `/press/` and `/cost-index/track-record/`, launch The Refusals, publish the negative results, bind the handbook, build the Food Cost Grader. All are agent-executable with near-zero founder time, and traffic + consumer confidence is exactly what a pre-product company can bank. THE GREATS (trust-rituals) even reframes the debt as the asset: the 72 falsehoods 'are not a scandal, they are the best story the company has — all 72 were true on publication day, they broke from a deliberate methodology upgrade, and Muntin found them itself,' and the archive's unflattering interior (26 frozen series, 97.6% reconstructed, 10,294 revisions, 37 refusals) 'is the moat.'
contradictions.sideB: THE GREATS (traffic-engine) and THE OPERATOR (domain-correctness) both say amplification before correction is negative-value. traffic-engine: 'in an answer-engine world a published number is not read once and discarded; it is ingested, attributed, and repeated at machine speed. Every citation-capture move in this list multiplies whatever is on the page' — and the multiplier currently applies to ≥72 false claims and a cite drawer that invites verification against a gate that does not exist. domain-correctness makes correctness a gating milestone, not a parallel track: 'run one real month end-to-end on Tacombi's own invoices and counts, and have a working restaurant CPA review the output… before opening the bookkeeper channel.'
contradictions.whyItMatters: The resolution decides whether the next quarter is agent-shaped or founder-shaped. Amplification is nearly all agent work with zero founder-hours and produces the metric the founder asked for. Correction is mostly founder-blocked — the Purchases contract re-derivation, a location-attribution product decision, a CPA review, one real month on Tacombi's data, and the founder's call on whether to correct-in-place or retract the July dispatch. Note also that trust-rituals and traffic-engine disagree about the SAME 72 falsehoods: one wants them cleared before amplifying, the other wants them published as the flagship trust artifact. Those two resolve differently and produce different pages, but they share one prerequisite neither foundation disputes — an append-only corrections ledger with a 'gate added' field, which does not exist and whose enabling gate (`check-src-sentinel.mjs`, named 'rung 0' by the founder ten days ago) is absent from disk.

contradictions.tension: 'No submitters' is the strongest and most constitutional sentence on the site — and the highest-leverage growth mechanism proposed is a submitter lane.
contradictions.sideA: THE GREATS (branded-index) wants the clause elevated to a headline claim with its own anchor and a constitutional ADR: 'no market participant submits a price to us is a stronger and more checkable claim than anything else on the site,' and 'the no-submitters clause is not boilerplate; it is the precise architectural difference between SOFR and LIBOR.' free-authority pushes further, proposing a Consumer-Reports-style No Commercial Use clause forbidding any vendor from citing a reading in advertising — 'a promise made before there was any money to refuse.'
contradictions.sideB: THE GREATS (traffic-engine) names an operator-contributed lane as the Levels.fyi flywheel and the answer to the archive's real weakness: 'Open the contribution seam on the 142 ingredient pages as a separate, clearly-labeled what operators report paying lane — delivered price, vendor category, pack size, month, region — never merged into the wholesale index.' Its argument is that the reconstructable public backfill is not a moat, but operator-reported delivered prices are: 'they are the gap between the wholesale reference and the invoice, which is precisely the question Vendor Benchmark exists to answer and precisely the number no public feed contains.' The moderated pipeline (`/api/submission/create` → admin decide → publish-data) is already built and has published zero rows.
contradictions.whyItMatters: An operator is a market participant. The moment operators submit prices, the site's strongest sentence needs a caveat, and a caveated architectural claim is a weaker instrument than an absolute one — LIBOR's lesson is that an index dies from architecture, not from a bad print. The fence traffic-engine proposes (separate lane, n-threshold withholding, never merged into the measured tier) may hold technically and still not hold rhetorically for the skeptical trade editor branded-index is writing for. The fork also has a capacity edge: the contribution lane creates a recurring founder moderation obligation ('approving submitted prices is a judgement call with fact-gate consequences, and it must not be delegated') in a company at a 2.7x deficit — and it is the only proposal in the whole register that converts a growth mechanism into a permanent human queue. Deciding this now is cheap; deciding it after the first submission is not.

contradictions.tension: Which invoices get seeded from the founder's own shift — the broadliners the market has, or the specialty distributors the corpus has — and which Don is the company designing around.
contradictions.sideA: THE GREATS (activation-retention) and THE OPERATOR (the-decision) both make the cold start the top priority and both name broadliners: 'Clear the /try gate with ten real invoices from Don's own shift… Treat this as the highest-priority item in either repo,' and 'seed it from the top ten broadliner layouts before the first customer arrives — the same corpus that clears the /try gate.' The logic is that a stranger's first upload is most likely a Sysco or US Foods invoice, and `needs_review` blocks `/post`, so a first upload that does not auto-confirm becomes manual data entry with extra steps.
contradictions.sideB: THE OPERATOR (incumbent-customer, the-day) says the corpus contains zero broadliner invoices and the beachhead is the opposite: the top ten vendors by volume are I. Halper Paper, Chefs' Warehouse, Baldor, Pat LaFrieda, Edward Don, Fresco, the Montgomery County Department of Liquor Control, Cintas, Staples and Cozzini Bros. 'Reorder the vendor seed and the template roadmap to lead with the specialty long tail… with the broadliners as a second wave.' Its argument is that broadliners are 'precisely the invoices every incumbent already handles well via EDI, and precisely the invoices absent from the only real corpus the company has.'
contradictions.whyItMatters: These consume the same irreplaceable resource — hours of the founder's hands on real invoices — and they cannot both go first. The decision-panel plan is not executable as written: Don cannot seed broadliner layouts from a shift whose corpus contains none, so 'ten real invoices from Don's own shift' produces specialty templates, not the ones `/try` was gated on. Underneath sits a three-way conflict about Don himself that no foundation resolves. operator-the-day says stop designing around him — 'biased on capture format, on vendor mix, on technical fluency, and on purchasing authority simultaneously,' and `first-try-reliability-roadmap.md` §4d already says the Tacombi corpus is not the demo population. operator-the-decision and domain-correctness say the three blocking acts are all things only he can do (seed templates, run one real month, phone the firms). And branded-index says the one-person fact is load-bearing evidence for the index's independence and must stay on the methodology page — against `founder-vision.md`'s recorded pivot, 'I worry that if people know it's just me, they'll discount the product.'

contradictions.tension: The Spanish half: narrow-and-finish the whole corpus, or split it and freeze the prose.
contradictions.sideA: THE OPERATOR (spanish-operator) says do NOT freeze: keep `/es/cost-index/` (143 pages, 0% retired), `/es/library/` and `/es/tools/` intact, retire only the 25 still-indexed retired-web-SEO pages and 12 retired sheets, and re-aim the surface from the kitchen to the owner-and-her-contadora with `/para-tu-contadora` as the ES conversion destination. Its evidence: `copy.es.ts` carries 2,459 translated strings (94.5% of EN) with 1.0% verbatim-English; Square shipped its full ecosystem in Spanish in 2022, proving Spanish-preferring owner-operators are a reachable software-buying population, while QBO US has no Spanish UI and no Spanish was found for MarginEdge, R365 or xtraCHEF — the back-office layer is unserved.
contradictions.sideB: THE GREATS (traffic-engine) says split it: invest in `/es/cost-index/` (143), `/es/tools/` and the funnel pages, and FREEZE `/es/library/` (221) and `/es/glossary/` (172) at current state — 'a price page needs almost no translation maintenance because the number regenerates from the same source, while an essay needs re-translation on every edit.' THE BONES back the cost side: `es/` is 19,547 of 72,757 file-touches (26.9%), the largest tree in the repo's churn, priced at ~3 h/mo of a 53 h/mo ledger, and `check-locale-parity` is a site-wide ratchet obligating an ES page for every EN one.
contradictions.whyItMatters: Both sides reject the two simple answers and disagree only about the prose corpus — but that is 393 pages, the churn driver, and the difference between a scoped parity gate and a site-wide one. The measured funnel facts make the disagreement urgent rather than academic: 2 of 651 ES pages carry a waitlist form, 384 ES pages carry a subscribe box of which exactly one sends the `source` value the broadcast worker accepts, and zero ES editions of the dispatch exist against 4 EN. So every ES page currently promises `un correo mensual` that has never once been sent in Spanish.
